analysis: This PR batch has only documentation changes: a new changelog.d entry and an update to docs/provider/cli-reference.md, which adds a paragraph near line 179 and bumps the date. No source code is included. The prose says that when `darkbloom restart` or `darkbloom update` has drained and stopped the provider but the relaunch fails (e.g. `loadService` throws), crash recovery (the watchdog) is re-armed. It cites ServiceDrain+Recovery.swift (`ServiceDrain.relaunchDrainedProvider`), which is not supplied, so I could not verify the described behavior. A drain timeout still leaves recovery disabled. Relevant threats: T-043 (the watchdog and rollback authority are the same replaceable binary) and T-057 (stranded provider availability). Re-arming the watchdog after a failed relaunch plausibly improves availability and adds no new trust grant. It also interacts with lifecycle/update lease and logout semantics: logout disables recovery, and the logout docs say a drain left closed keeps recovery disabled. Those are unchanged. The next pass should check the real Swift change. Items to verify: that re-arming happens only on relaunch failure, not on drain timeout or logout; that it respects `provider.auto_restart`; that it does not restore the watchdog while the credential lifecycle lock is held for logout; and that it does not re-arm after an intentional `stop`. No documentation-only security regression found.
